display.title: Judge Every Yid Favorably: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and the Secret Giver of Berditchev
display.summary_short: After Simchas Torah and on the yahrzeit of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, the storyteller shows how to see the good in every Jew, through the story of a rich man everyone thought was stingy.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins with Simchas Torah: we dance with the Torah closed because the Torah belongs equally to every Jew, and every Jewish soul has its own letter in the Torah. On the week of the yahrzeit of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, he tells how that tzaddik always spoke well of every Jew, praising a wagon driver who greased his wheels while wearing tallis and tefillin, and defending before Hashem a man who ate on Yom Kippur but would not lie about it. Then the main story: Shimon, the richest man in Berditchev, was known as stingy, and when he died the burial society wanted his family to pay double. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak refused, attended the funeral, and then revealed three stories: Shimon secretly replaced a wine merchant's lost money, quietly supported a poor family whose father had gone away to find work, and refused to take back a loan because "Hashem, the guarantor" had already repaid him. Each time he would not accept repayment. Shimon gave his tzedakah in secret, the best way.
display.lesson: Never judge a Jew by how he looks from the outside; always judge favorably. Tzedakah given in secret is the greatest kind.
